bibl.title: The Twelth Catechetical Homily — ܡܐܡܪܐ ܕܬܖ̈ܝܢ
The first homily on baptism
bibl.author: Theodore of Mopsuestia — ܬܐܕܘܪܘܤ ܡܦܫܩܢܐ

noteGrp.note: Addresses the idea of sacraments in general and explains the meaning of baptismal enrolment and exorcisms. The sacrament consists of the symbols and signs of the invisible reality and thus they are in need of interpretation. Since the church is the symbol of heavenly realities in this world, those who are in the Church also have a relationship with heaven. The candidates enrolled for baptism are enrolled in heaven as citizens of heavenly Jerusalem. Exorcisms are necessary because the freedom from Satan, which catechumens are going to receive in baptism, makes the devil fight against them with even greater strength. Theodore describes exorcisms as a lawsuit between a candidate and Satan.
